chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban from Salamah from Abu Abdillah from his father that the Commander of the Faithful used to cut the hand of the thief for a quarter of a dinar.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ المُؤمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.يَقطَعُ: He cuts (referring to cutting the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of stolen goods required for cutting the hand in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Tusi’s *al-Istibsar*, establishes the *nisab* (minimum threshold) for *hadd* amputation at a quarter of a dinar, tracing the ruling through a chain of transmission back to Imam al-Sadiq and ultimately to Ali ibn Abi Talib. This attribution to the Commander of the Faithful highlights the early juristic consensus in Shia tradition regarding the valuation of currency for criminal penalties, distinguishing it from other schools that may use different standards such as the dinar or dirham directly.
